newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian group plans West Africa trade mission.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian group plans West Africa trade mission.

text.p: A Nigerian business group said on Friday it was embarking on a trade mission to West African countries to explore the market in a move to reduce the large stock of goods in the country's warehouses.

"With the stock inventory in the nation's manufacturing warehouses mounting to over six billion naira ($75 million), the need to exploit business opportuinities in West African countries has become imperative now more than ever before," Sam Ohanbunwa, chairman of the Business Club Ikeja, told reporters in Lagos.
The mission is expected to begin from September 30 and will take the group first to Ghana and Sierra Leone, he added.
Finance minister Anthony Ani during his half-year performance of the 1996 budget in August called on manufacturers to look beyond the domestic market to reduce finished goods in the warehouses.

Nigeria's economy, the largest in Sub-Saharan Africa, has been mired in recession since a rash of strikes, riots and government policy turnarounds followed the annulment of a presidential election in 1993 that was to restore democracy.
Ohanbunwa said: "The trip also has the objective of stimulating the implementation of trade enhancing protocols of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)."
He said members of the group would meet with government and business leaders in both countries to share a vision on a common market for the sub-region.
"It is the way to ensure an effective penetration of the West African market by Nigerian businessmen."
ECOWAS was founded in the 1980s by 16 West African countries to integrate the sub-regional markets for a sustained economic growth and development.
Although official trade between them is little, unoffficial trade is booming with market women travelling with bundles of goods along the borders.
